headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage and capability conflict: unstructured can read/write and egress allowlisted data, while godot_rl_agents is local-only game-playing with no shared channel documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and unstructured. A has no I/O surfaces or network egress, while B’s documented file/API handling does not imply it ingests A’s outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies A’s text output into B’s prompt or input files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared clipboard, queue, or MCP bridge is added between them, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate processes with no shared clipboard.
Do not pipe A’s output directly into B’s parser.
Use explicit schema validation on any handoff file.
Add provenance labels to all intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: introduce a broker that strips instructions from A’s outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read files and egress to allowlisted network destinations, so if it processes sensitive documents from a shared workspace it may transmit content outward. A is local game-playing with no network egress, so it is not the leakage source; the pair risk comes from B handling data that A does not constrain. This is plausible in default document-processing setups.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in a workspace B can read, leakage risk exists.
IF B sends extracted content to its allowlisted APIs, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Restrict B to a non-sensitive test directory.
Disable outbound API calls for B where possible.
Review allowlisted endpoints before running B.
Separate A and B workspaces.
requires-engineering: add content redaction before any network call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no filesystem or network write capability, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with B. B can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without a documented shared writable target or locking issue, the overlap is limited. The pairwise conflict pathway is therefore small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state without locks, B can overwrite artifacts.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Make A outputs read-only.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a document processor that can consume files and produce downstream outputs, so if A’s outputs are handed to B without verification, errors can cascade. A is not documented as producing authoritative facts, which lowers severity, but the handoff still exists if an orchestrator treats A’s output as input. Uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF A’s output is fed into B without validation, B may propagate mistakes.
IF B is used to generate reports or extracted text from A’s artifacts, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Validate A outputs against a schema before B consumes them.
Compare B outputs against source documents.
Log provenance for each transformed field.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show regulated data classes or residency constraints. B has privacy-policy and API references, but no concrete mismatch with A is documented. The compliance pathway is therefore limited to future deployment choices rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s document pipeline, compliance review is needed.
IF deployment regions or retention policies differ, a mismatch could arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Review B’s privacy policy before deployment.
Document retention settings.
Keep processing local for sensitive inputs.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
